insider_note: Here A multiplies the DERIVATIVE of the denominator, the opposite of the split in which A multiplies the denominator itself — either labelling is legitimate, so always re-read which coefficient is being solved for rather than assuming a fixed layout.

steps.label: Write the numerator as A·Dr′ + B·Dr + C and solve for A, B, C
lines: Coeff of cosx: A+B=1, coeff of sinx:
steps.why: The layout here swaps A and B's roles compared with the split in which A multiplies the denominator itself — A multiplies the denominator's derivative this time — but the method is identical: match sinx, cosx, and the constant term.
common_mistakes: Assuming A multiplies Dr here as it does in the other layout, without re-reading which coefficient this question actually assigns to which part.
Sign slip solving A+B=1 and −A+B=3 together (adding gives 2B=4, so B=2, then A=1−B=−1).
steps.memory_tip: A+B=1 and −A+B=3 added together gives 2B=4 directly — the fastest way to solve this particular pair.

steps.label: Substitute back and split the integral into three parts
steps.why: With A=−1 multiplying the log term, B=2 multiplying the plain x term, and C=5 left over on the genuine ∫dx/Dr piece, the split works exactly as in the earlier three-part example, roles relabelled.
common_mistakes: Putting the wrong sign on the log term — A=−1 makes this term NEGATIVE, unlike the earlier example where the log coefficient was positive.
Forgetting to carry C=5 as a multiplier on the remaining integral.
steps.memory_tip: A is negative here, so the log term in the final answer is subtracted, not added — check the sign before boxing the result.

steps.label: Reduce the remaining integral by the tan(x/2) substitution
steps.why: This denominator collapses to the same simple (1+t) form as 1+sinx+cosx, since cosx+sinx+1 is algebraically the same shape — only the order of the terms differs.
common_mistakes: Not recognising this as the same simplification the 1+sinx+cosx denominator already needs, and re-deriving it with unnecessary extra steps.
Losing the modulus bars on log|1+t|.
steps.memory_tip: cosx+sinx+1 IS 1+sinx+cosx, just written in a different order — the same (1+t) simplification applies.

steps.label: Combine for the final answer
steps.why: Multiplying C=5 by the log|1+t| just found and writing t back as tan(x/2) gives the third and final term, completing the answer in x.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply C=5 into the log|1+t| result.
Combining the two different logs — log|cosx+sinx+1| and log|1+tan(x/2)| — into one, which they cannot be since their arguments are different.
steps.memory_tip: Two DIFFERENT logs appear in this answer — one in x, one in tan(x/2) — they never combine into a single log term.
